plan.title: Whole-blood case/control subgroup discovery by consensus clustering
plan.analytical_narrative: The question asks whether the 120-sample whole-blood case/control cohort contains subgroups beyond the known two-condition split, and how stable they are. Because the input is raw Salmon gene-level counts with 60 replicates per group and no batch variable, the plan follows the population-scale bulk RNA-seq clustering procedure: (1) blind vst sample-structure QC to see whether condition or technical variables dominate the primary variance axes and to flag outliers before any clustering; (2) a minimal filterByExpr low-count filter with TMM normalization, producing a centered matrix of the top 2000 most variable variance-stabilized genes — the stated input for consensus clustering per R-0142@c982; (3) ConsensusClusterPlus with 1000 resampling iterations at 80% item subsampling, k from 2 to 8, selecting k jointly on the consensus CDF delta area and the proportion of ambiguous clustering (PAC), and tabulating any recovered clusters against condition and library size to detect confounded clusters; (4) a final report that states every input, method, and stability evidence element, with a reproducibility record. Consensus clustering is known to return clusters on random data (doi:10.1038/srep06207), so the plan treats any subgroup beyond case/control as a hypothesis requiring external support, and states that caution in the report. NMF metagene discovery (tool of record for gene programs) is absent from the package pool, so PCA loadings are used descriptively only if needed.

TMM normalization (edgeR) with median-of-ratios size factors stated
